intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart from Porto Vromi or Skinari Cape and include swimming stops in sea caves.

experiences.name: Athens Street Food Tour in Monastiraki
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Monastiraki and Psiri neighborhoods on a self-guided or guided street food tour. Sample souvlaki, spanakopita, loukoumades (honey donuts), fresh gyros, and local cheeses from market stalls and traditional tavernas. The Central Market (Varvakios Agora) nearby is perfect for discovering local ingredients and authentic Greek flavors.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand caused by crushed coral and its shallow, crystal-clear lagoon waters. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, snorkel in warm turquoise waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class & Market Visit
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania where a local chef guides you through preparing authentic Cretan dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and bougatsa (cream-filled pastry). The class begins with a visit to the local market to source fresh ingredients, giving you deep insight into the Mediterranean diet and Cretan culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Seafood Dinner in Santorini
experiences.description: Board a small catamaran or sailboat from Ammoudi Bay for a sunset cruise around the Santorini caldera. Swim in the volcanic hot springs, snorkel in clear Aegean waters, and enjoy a freshly prepared onboard seafood meal with local wine as you watch the legendary Santorini sunset paint the sky in gold and orange hues.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange budget airport transfer or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the property. Grab a light snack from a nearby late-night kiosk or the hotel reception if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a local kiosk or periptero (street kiosk) near the resort – gyros wrap or tiropita (cheese pie) for under €3

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-book a shared airport shuttle to save money vs. a private taxi. Have euros in cash ready for small purchases. Rest well for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a slow walk along the beachfront directly accessible from Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm June sea and scout the area – locate the nearest bus stops, minimarkets, and tavernas for budget planning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on the resort's beach or the nearest public beach. Swim in the warm sea (average 24–25°C in June), sunbathe, and relax. Explore the immediate coastal strip on foot and find a local bakery or mini-market for affordable snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village or town center. Browse the waterfront promenade, watch the sunset, and settle into a casual local taverna for your first proper Greek dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh koulouri (sesame bread ring) and a freddo espresso from a local bakery – around €2–3 total
meals.lunch: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and a cold Mythos beer from a beachside kiosk – around €5
meals.dinner: Local taverna: Greek salad (€5), grilled sardines (€7), and house wine carafe (€4) – total around €16 per person

day_by_day.notes: June 16 is your first full day. Keep it relaxed to beat jet lag. Public beaches in Greece are free – avoid paying for sun loungers by bringing a towel from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a cheap bicycle to explore a nearby traditional village inland. Walk through narrow whitewashed alleyways, visit the central plateia (square), and peek into a small Orthodox church – free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a quieter, less-touristy beach cove accessible by bus or a short hike. With only 8mm of rain expected all month and hot sunny skies, this is perfect for snorkeling. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible (or rent cheaply locally) to explore the clear warm water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Find a local souvlaki or gyros stand for a cheap, filling dinner. Walk the harbor or marina area if nearby and enjoy the warm evening air.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café – around €3
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a bakery: tiropita, loukoumades (honey doughnuts), and water – around €4
meals.dinner: Souvlaki wrap with pita, tzatziki, and fries from a local grill house – around €4–5

day_by_day.notes: Local KTEL buses are very affordable (usually €1–3 per ride). Ask at the hotel reception for the nearest bus stop and timetable. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water – it will be around 29°C.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the nearest archaeological site or ancient ruins in the region – most charge €4–10 entry and are stunning in the morning light before the heat peaks. Explore at your own pace; free audio guides are sometimes available via QR code on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a shaded local market (laiki agora) if one is running nearby. Browse fresh produce, olives, local cheeses, and honey. Buy picnic supplies for a beach lunch. Head to the beach for a long afternoon swim and relaxation session.
day_by_day.evening: Cook-in or picnic evening: use your market purchases to assemble a simple spread of bread, olives, tomatoes, feta, and fruit on the beach or in your room. Save money for a bigger splurge later in the trip.

meals.breakfast: Bougatsa (custard or cheese pastry) and Greek coffee at a local café – around €3
meals.lunch: Self-assembled market picnic on the beach: feta, olives, crusty bread, cherry tomatoes – around €5
meals.dinner: Picnic continuation or a simple mezze spread from the market – around €5–7

day_by_day.notes: Local markets (laiki) usually run Tuesday and Friday mornings in most Greek towns. Check with hotel staff for the nearest one. Buying local produce is extremely cheap and a great way to eat like a local.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim at sunrise on the beach – magical in June with calm seas. After swimming, take a walk along the coastal path and look for sea urchins and small fish in the rock pools. Pack a light bag for a day trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget day trip by local bus or ferry to a nearby island or coastal town. Explore the new area, walk the harbor, and visit a free viewpoint or hilltop for panoramic sea views. Spend time on the local beach.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in the day-trip destination before catching the last bus or ferry back. Try the local specialty of the area – ask locals what the town is known for.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go from a bakery near the bus station – cheese pie and juice – around €3
meals.lunch: Freshly caught grilled fish of the day at a harbor-side taverna in the day-trip town – around €10–12
meals.dinner: Octopus meze and a glass of local wine at a small family-run ouzeri – around €10

day_by_day.notes: Check return bus/ferry times carefully before you leave to avoid being stranded. Carry cash as smaller islands and towns may not accept cards everywhere.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at the resort beach. Take a long swim, practice snorkeling, or simply read under the sun. The hot, sunny weather makes this a perfect low-effort beach morning. Apply sunscreen generously – UV index is high in June.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or paddleboard from a local beach rental shop (usually €8–15/hour) and explore the coastline from the water. Alternatively, join a free or cheap group beach volleyball game if organized at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local restaurant strip. Try a traditional Greek meze dinner – order several small sharing plates instead of a main course to try more dishes for less money.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit salad and Greek yogurt from a beach café – around €4
meals.lunch: Dakos (Cretan rusk salad with tomato and feta) and cold water at a beach taverna – around €6
meals.dinner: Meze dinner: taramasalata, melitzanosalata, dolmades, and pita bread shared between two – around €12–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Meze-style dining is one of the best budget strategies in Greece – you get variety and quantity for a reasonable price. Always ask for the daily specials (piato tis imeras) which are usually cheaper.

day_by_day.morning: Midway point of the trip! Take a scenic coastal hike along a marked trail near the resort. June is ideal for hiking – start early (7–9am) before peak heat. Look for wild herbs like thyme and oregano along the path, and enjoy sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reward yourself after the hike with a long beach afternoon. Find a secluded cove if possible – ask locals or hotel staff for their secret spots. Swim, nap, and recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the halfway point with a slightly more indulgent dinner at a well-reviewed local taverna. Order the fresh catch of the day and a bottle of local wine to share.

meals.breakfast: Eggs, tomatoes, and olives at a traditional kafeneio (old-style Greek café) – around €4
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from the minimarket for the hike: nuts, dried fruit, and water – around €3
meals.dinner: Grilled sea bream or sea bass, Greek salad, and a bottle of house white wine – around €20–22 per person (a modest splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Carry at least 1.5 liters of water per person on the hike. Wear sturdy sandals or light trail shoes. Start the hike before 9am to avoid the worst of the 29°C heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fishing village nearby. Watch the fishermen bring in the morning catch (usually 6–8am), chat with locals, and browse the small harbor. This is authentic Greece at its best and completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at one of the area's most scenic beaches. With warm, clear water and sunny skies, this is a prime day for underwater photography if you have a waterproof camera or phone case.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local psarotaverna (fish tavern) in the fishing village for ultra-fresh seafood at lower prices than tourist-facing restaurants. Order whatever the fishermen brought in that morning.

meals.breakfast: Freshly baked bread and local honey from the village bakery – around €2–3
meals.lunch: Grilled calamari and a cold Alfa beer at a beachside spot – around €8
meals.dinner: Psarotaverna dinner: fish soup (kakavia), grilled mullet, and house wine – around €14–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fishing villages are often a short bus ride or taxi share away. The further from the main tourist strip, the cheaper and more authentic the food. Ask hotel staff for their personal recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walking tour of the nearest town or city. Download a free walking tour app (like GPSmyCity) or use Google Maps to find key landmarks: old town, Byzantine church, Venetian or Ottoman architecture depending on the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local museum – most regional Greek museums charge €4–8 and are fascinating. Alternatively, explore a free archaeological open-air site. Spend the late afternoon cooling off with a swim back at the resort beach.
day_by_day.evening: Try cooking a Greek meal yourself – buy ingredients from the local market and prepare a simple Greek dinner in the room if facilities allow, or enjoy a casual souvlaki dinner out.

meals.breakfast: Freddo cappuccino and a croissant at a local café – around €3.50
meals.lunch: Gyros pita with all toppings from a local grill – around €3–4, one of the best budget meals in Greece
meals.dinner: Homemade or taverna: moussaka and a glass of local red wine – around €9–11

day_by_day.notes: Many Greek museums offer free entry on the first Sunday of the month and for EU students under 25. Check the specific museum's policy before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning with a focus on relaxation. Try a yoga or stretching session on the sand at sunrise. The warm June mornings are perfect for this. Alternatively, take a slow swim along the shoreline for light exercise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a different stretch of coastline by taking a cheap local bus to a nearby beach town. Walk the promenade, browse local shops for affordable souvenirs (olive oil soap, honey, herbs, small ceramics), and enjoy the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Join locals at a waterfront kafeneio for an evening of people-watching. Order a Greek coffee, a freddo espresso, or an ouzo with complimentary mezedes (small snacks). This is how Greeks spend their evenings.

meals.breakfast: Loukoumades (honey-drenched doughnuts) from a street vendor – around €3 for a portion
meals.lunch: Fresh tomato and feta salad with crusty bread at a beach café – around €6
meals.dinner: Lamb chops (paidakia) with roasted potatoes and tzatziki at a local grill taverna – around €13–15

day_by_day.notes: Souvenir shopping tip: avoid shops directly on the main tourist drag. Walk one or two streets back and prices drop significantly. Olive oil products and local honey make excellent cheap gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip – look for cheap shared boat excursions (€15–25) that visit sea caves, hidden beaches, or snorkeling spots. These are usually bookable through local agencies or directly at the harbor. Book the day before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion or return to shore and spend the afternoon at the most beautiful beach you've discovered so far on the trip. This is your penultimate full beach day – make the most of it.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a rooftop or sea-view restaurant for sunset dinner. Order the house special and a local wine. Watch the golden Greek sunset over the Aegean – one of the most beautiful sights in the world.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with honey, granola, and fresh figs at a café – around €4
meals.lunch: Snacks and water on the boat (bring from a minimarket to save money) – around €3
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner: stuffed peppers or pastitsio (Greek pasta bake) with a carafe of rosé wine – around €16–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shared boat trips are one of the best value experiences in Greece. Always negotiate or compare prices between two or three operators at the harbor before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning. Swim, snorkel, and soak in the last full day of sun. Take photos, collect a small pebble or shell as a free memento. Reflect on the trip over a long, slow Greek breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration: revisit your favorite spot from the trip, buy any remaining souvenirs, or try a food or experience you haven't had yet. Consider a final hike to a viewpoint for panoramic photos.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite taverna from the trip. Order generously and enjoy your last Greek meal. Try a dessert: galaktoboureko (custard pastry) or baklava with Greek coffee.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a café: eggs, olives, feta, tomatoes, bread, and coffee – around €6–7
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch: hummus, pita, and a cold beer – around €7
meals.dinner: Farewell feast: mixed grill platter, Greek salad, tzatziki, wine, and dessert – around €20–22 per person (final splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to avoid rushing tomorrow morning. Set aside any remaining euros for airport expenses. Check if your hotel offers a late checkout option.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning final swim if time allows – a perfect send-off. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at reception if your flight is later in the day. Take a last walk along the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final cheap lunch near the hotel or airport area. Head to the airport with plenty of time. Spend remaining euros on Greek products at the airport (olive oil, herbs, wine) – duty-free is sometimes cheaper than tourist shops.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with memories of warm seas, fresh seafood, golden sunsets, and authentic local flavors. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Greek coffee and a cheese pie from a bakery near the hotel – around €3
meals.lunch: Gyros wrap for the road – around €4
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport check-in during peak June travel season. Keep a small amount of euros for airport bus, taxi, or last-minute purchases. Greece requires no departure tax for EU/international flights – check your airline's baggage policy to avoid surprise fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and take a pre-arranged airport transfer or taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the resort grounds to get oriented.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the departure airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at the resort bar or a quick gyros wrap from a nearby 24-hour souvlaki kiosk near the hotel (budget-friendly, ~€5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – arrival is late at night. Confirm resort check-in is prepared for a late arrival. Set up your room and get a good night's rest to prepare for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Afterward, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront promenade directly in front of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea and find your perfect spot on the beach to settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a sun lounger on the resort's private beach and spend the afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear warm water. Try snorkeling if equipment is available at the resort. Explore the immediate beach area and nearby coves on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest village or harbor for your first real Greek dinner. Stroll the waterfront and pick a traditional taverna with outdoor seating and sea views.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet – enjoy Greek yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, and pastries
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at the resort beach bar – try a Greek salad (horiatiki) and fresh-squeezed lemonade (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna in the nearby village – order grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh bread, and a carafe of local house wine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is your orientation and recovery day. Don't over-plan – let yourself ease into the Greek pace of life. Sunscreen is essential; UV index is very high in June.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, join a half-day boat tour or water taxi departing from the local harbor. Explore nearby sea caves, hidden coves, and secluded beaches only accessible by boat. Swim in turquoise waters off the boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore by early afternoon. Visit a local beach market or artisan stalls near the harbor. Browse handmade ceramics, olive wood products, and local spices. Take a siesta back at the resort during the hottest part of the day (2–4 PM).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local village on foot at dusk when temperatures cool. Visit a traditional kafeneion (Greek coffee house) for a freddo espresso or Greek coffee, and watch locals play backgammon.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – try spanakopita (spinach pie) if available
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the boat tour or a quick bite at a harbor-side café – try tiropita (cheese pie) and a cold Mythos beer (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Family-run mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) in the village – order a spread of small dishes: dolmades, taramasalata, saganaki, and grilled sardines (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat tour the evening before or at the harbor in the morning. Tours typically depart at 9–10 AM and return by 1–2 PM. Bring a hat, reef-safe sunscreen, and water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV from a local rental shop (widely available near most Greek beach resorts, ~€25–40/day) and head out to explore the coastline independently. Drive to a more remote beach away from the resort crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the remote beach you discovered. Swim, relax, and enjoy the solitude. Pack a picnic of local bread, olives, cheese, and tomatoes purchased from a village bakery or mini-market in the morning.
day_by_day.evening: Return scooters by sunset. Walk up to a hilltop viewpoint or a nearby chapel with panoramic views to watch the spectacular Greek sunset. Return to the resort area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local village bakery (fournos) for fresh koulouri (sesame bread ring), bougatsa (custard pastry), and Greek coffee (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Self-made picnic on the remote beach – local cheese (feta or graviera), olives, tomatoes, crusty bread, and bottled water (~€8–12 from a mini-market)
meals.dinner: Seaside restaurant near the resort – try fresh grilled fish of the day (ask for the catch), Greek salad, and local white wine such as Assyrtiko (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Carry a valid driving license for scooter rental. Stick to paved coastal roads and always wear a helmet. Fill up on fuel before heading to remote areas as petrol stations can be sparse.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby historic site or ancient ruins accessible by local bus or taxi. Explore the archaeological site in the cooler morning hours before the midday heat sets in. Hire a local audio guide or printed guide for context.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ruins, visit a nearby traditional village with whitewashed houses and bougainvillea-draped alleys. Wander freely, pop into local shops, and visit a small Byzantine church or monastery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a swim at the beach or the resort pool. Get ready for a slightly more upscale dinner to treat yourself mid-trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Village taverna near the ruins – try moussaka or pastitsio (Greek baked pasta) with a cold beer or sparkling water (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated restaurant near the resort – try lamb kleftiko (slow-baked lamb) or stuffed peppers with rice, paired with a glass of Nemea red wine (~€30–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check local bus schedules the night before or arrange a taxi in advance. Most archaeological sites open at 8 AM and close at 3–8 PM depending on the season. Entrance fees are typically €6–12.

day_by_day.morning: Join a morning cooking class offered by a local Greek family or a cooking school in the area. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as tzatziki, spanakopita, and a main course. This is a hands-on, intimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the lunch you cooked during the class. Afterward, return to the beach for a long, lazy afternoon swim and sunbathing session. June afternoons are perfect – warm sea, light breeze, and golden light.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local harbor at sunset to watch fishing boats return with the day's catch. Chat with fishermen if possible. Choose a harborside restaurant and order the freshest catch of the evening.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Eat what you cooked during the cooking class – included in the class price (~€45–65 per person for the full experience)
meals.dinner: Harbor taverna – fresh fish or seafood pasta, a Greek salad, and local retsina or white wine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2–3 days in advance. Ask the resort concierge for recommendations on reputable local cooking experiences. Classes typically run 3–4 hours in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full rest and rejuvenation morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and then spend time at the resort beach or pool. Read a book, do some journaling, or simply soak up the sun. This is your midpoint rest day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle kayak or paddleboard session along the coastline (rentals available at most beach resorts, ~€10–15/hour). Paddle to a nearby cove or sea arch if accessible.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday evenings in Greek villages are lively. Head into town for a volta (the traditional Greek evening stroll). Join locals walking the main street, stop for ice cream (pagoto) at a gelateria, and enjoy the festive atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast – try everything, including loukoumades (honey doughnuts) if available
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch – club sandwich, fresh fruit juice, and a Greek salad (~€14–18)
meals.dinner: Casual village square restaurant – try souvlaki platters, tzatziki, pita, and chips with a cold Alfa or Mythos beer (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally relaxed – a balanced trip needs downtime. Don't feel guilty about doing very little today. The slower pace is part of the authentic Greek experience (siga-siga – slowly, slowly).

day_by_day.morning: Organize a day trip to a nearby island or peninsula by ferry or speedboat (check local tour operators). Spend the morning on the boat ride enjoying sea views and arriving at your destination refreshed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip destination – visit its main beach, a hilltop fortress or monastery, and the local market. Swim in a different stretch of the Aegean and compare it to your home beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return by late afternoon ferry or boat. Unwind at the resort with a sunset cocktail on the beach or at the resort bar. Enjoy a quieter dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Local taverna at the day-trip destination – try whatever the island specialty is, often fresh seafood or local pies (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or a nearby casual eatery – try dakos (Cretan rusk salad), grilled calamari, and local beer (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day trips to nearby islands are very popular in June – book tickets at least 1–2 days in advance. Ferries and speedboats often sell out on weekends and holidays. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local olive grove or winery for a guided tasting tour. Greece has a rich agricultural heritage and many producers welcome visitors. Learn about olive oil production or local grape varieties and sample products.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, head to a quieter, less-touristy beach recommended by locals. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing away from the main tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Visit the local weekly open-air market (laiki agora) if it falls on this day – ask the resort about market days. Buy fresh produce, local honey, herbs, and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with products purchased at the olive grove or winery – local bread, cheese, olives, and wine (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek home-style restaurant (estiatorio) – try a slow-cooked stifado (beef or rabbit stew) or roasted lamb with roasted potatoes and horta (wild greens) (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Olive grove and winery tours typically cost €10–20 per person and include tastings. Many will also sell bottles of olive oil and wine to take home – great authentic souvenirs within mid-range budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise walk or early morning hike on a coastal trail near the resort. The morning light and cooler temperatures make this the perfect time. Bring water and a light snack. Photograph the coastline and wildflowers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a leisurely afternoon exploring a nearby town or larger village. Visit a local museum (archaeological, folk, or maritime), browse boutique shops, and enjoy people-watching at a café.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural event if available – outdoor cinema, live Greek music (rebetiko or laïká), or a village festival (panigiri). Ask the resort concierge what's happening locally this week.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-hike snack (fruit, nuts, water) then a proper breakfast at a village café after the hike – Greek yogurt parfait and a frappe (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Town café or casual eatery – try a chicken gyros wrap with tzatziki and fries (~€7–10)
meals.dinner: If a village festival (panigiri) is on, eat from the communal food stalls – grilled meats, salads, and local wine for very reasonable prices (~€10–15). Otherwise, choose a local taverna (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Greek village festivals (panigiri) are magical, authentic experiences. They often happen on saints' name days and include live music, dancing, and communal feasting. Ask locals or the resort about any upcoming ones.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a water sports session. Try jet skiing, parasailing, or a banana boat ride at the beach – operators are usually set up on the main beach. Alternatively, book a beginner scuba diving lesson with a certified local dive center.
day_by_day.afternoon: After water sports, take a long, slow lunch and then relax on the beach. This is a great afternoon to simply float in the warm Aegean, read, and do nothing. Let the sun and sea restore you.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a rooftop bar or a clifftop restaurant for sundowner cocktails and dinner with a panoramic sea view. Splurge slightly for this special evening – it's near the end of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach taverna with your feet in the sand – grilled sea bream, Greek salad, and local white wine (~€25–32 per person)
meals.dinner: Rooftop or clifftop restaurant – try surf and turf or a seafood platter, paired with a bottle of local Assyrtiko white wine (~€35–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Water sports operators on the beach are generally safe and reputable but check for safety certifications. Scuba diving introductory dives (Discover Scuba) cost approximately €50–80 per person and are suitable for non-divers.

day_by_day.morning: Use the morning for last-minute beach time. Take a final long swim in the Aegean. Collect a few small pebbles or shells as natural mementos. Revisit your favorite spot on the beach for one last look.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon souvenir shopping. Look for: local thyme honey, saffron, mastiha products, handmade jewelry, ceramic tiles, and local spirits like ouzo or tsipouro. Focus on locally made, authentic items rather than mass-produced tourist goods.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip, or try somewhere new that you've had your eye on all week. Celebrate the trip with a full Greek feast.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – take your time and savor it
meals.lunch: Casual harbor café – a light mezedes spread with cold drinks (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a top local taverna – go all out with a full spread: starters, mains, dessert (loukoumades or baklava), and a bottle of wine (~€40–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: For souvenirs, avoid buying items labeled 'Made in China' – look for 'Made in Greece' or 'Handmade in Greece' labels. Spice shops, local delis, and artisan boutiques are better than tourist shops for authentic products.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise on the beach. Take photos, breathe in the sea air, and reflect on the trip. Return to the resort for a final breakfast. Begin packing and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure flight time, store luggage with the concierge if needed. Take a final walk through the village, stop for one last Greek coffee or frappe, and say goodbye to the places you've come to love.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport. Allow plenty of time for check-in and security. Board your departure flight home, carrying wonderful memories of Greece, a tan, and a suitcase full of local treasures.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – enjoy every bite
meals.lunch: Airport café or a quick souvlaki from a nearby kiosk before departure (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: On the flight home or at a transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM – confirm with the resort. Airport transfers should be pre-booked, especially if your flight departs in the afternoon or evening. Keep some euros for last-minute purchases or tips. Tip your favorite resort staff before leaving – it's greatly appreciated in Greece.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart from Porto Vromi or Skinari Cape and include swimming stops in sea caves.

experiences.name: Athens Street Food Tour in Monastiraki
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Monastiraki and Psiri neighborhoods on a self-guided or guided street food tour. Sample souvlaki, spanakopita, loukoumades (honey donuts), fresh gyros, and local cheeses from market stalls and traditional tavernas. The Central Market (Varvakios Agora) nearby is perfect for discovering local ingredients and authentic Greek flavors.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand caused by crushed coral and its shallow, crystal-clear lagoon waters. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, snorkel in warm turquoise waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort bar, and enjoy a light late-night snack before retiring.

meals.breakfast: On flight
meals.lunch: On flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome mezze platter and chilled Greek wine at the resort's lounge bar upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with the resort concierge. Request early check-in preparation so the room is fully ready upon late arrival. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take a relaxed orientation stroll along the resort's private beachfront, acclimating to the surroundings and soaking in the warm June sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's infinity pool or private beach. Arrange a complimentary snorkeling session through the resort to explore the crystal-clear waters. Enjoy light refreshments and fresh fruit from the poolside bar.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop or beachfront bar. Enjoy a premium welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, featuring contemporary Greek cuisine with locally sourced seafood.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Greek breakfast buffet at the resort – fresh pastries, local honey, Cretan cheeses, olives, fresh fruit, and Greek yogurt
meals.lunch: Light mezze and fresh grilled octopus at the poolside restaurant
meals.dinner: Signature tasting menu at the resort's fine-dining restaurant – grilled sea bass, lobster pasta, and baklava soufflé paired with Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. No heavy scheduling. Consult with the concierge to confirm bookings for the rest of the trip including boat tours and food experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided Athens city tour departing from the resort area. Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon with a licensed expert guide early in the morning to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Acropolis Museum afterward with skip-the-line tickets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Athens Street Food Tour in Monastiraki – explore the vibrant Monastiraki and Psiri neighborhoods on a premium guided street food tour. Sample spanakopita, souvlaki, loukoumades, fresh figs, and local cheeses from market vendors and artisan stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop dinner at a premium Athens restaurant with Acropolis views – enjoy modern Greek cuisine with a glass of local Nemea red wine as the Acropolis is illuminated at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with Aegean honey and walnuts, fresh orange juice, and espresso at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Guided street food tasting through Monastiraki – souvlaki wraps, tiropita, fresh pomegranate juice, and loukoumades with honey
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine-dining restaurant near Monastiraki – lamb chops with herb-infused orzo, grilled halloumi salad, and Greek walnut cake with mastiha ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and the street food tour well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Best to start the Acropolis visit by 8:00 AM to avoid peak heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter excursion from the local marina – sail along the stunning Aegean coastline, stopping at secluded coves and sea caves accessible only by water. Snorkeling equipment and paddleboards provided on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private boat charter to a pristine hidden beach for a swim and a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort's chef – served on the boat deck with chilled rosé wine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Indulge in a 90-minute couples' or solo spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa – choose from a traditional Greek olive oil massage or an Aegean sea salt body scrub. Light dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – eggs prepared to order, smoked salmon, Greek pastries, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the private boat – artisan bread, marinated olives, local cheeses, cured meats, fresh fruit, and chilled Santorini rosé
meals.dinner: Casual but refined dinner at the resort's beach taverna – grilled prawns, village salad, and fresh-baked pita with tzatziki

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 3 days in advance through the concierge. Apply high-SPF sunscreen generously. Bring a light cover-up and sunhat for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Elafonissi Beach – depart early by private luxury vehicle to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete (if the resort is Crete-based) or arrange a scenic seaplane or helicopter transfer for a truly premium experience. Arrive to enjoy the famous pink-tinged sand and turquoise lagoon in the early morning calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at Elafonissi – swim in the shallow pink-sand lagoon, explore the small island accessible by foot through the shallow water, and relax on a premium sun lounger with parasol arranged through the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by private transfer. Freshen up and enjoy a sunset dinner at a local seaside taverna near the resort, known for its traditional Cretan recipes and fresh-caught fish.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure – yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a charming beachside taverna near Elafonissi – grilled fish of the day, dakos (Cretan rusk salad), and local white wine
meals.dinner: Traditional Cretan taverna dinner near the resort – slow-cooked lamb with stamnagathi greens, kalitsounia cheese pies, and local Cretan raki to finish

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is best visited early to avoid crowds. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the delicate pink-sand ecosystem. The pink color is most vivid in morning light. Wear water shoes as the lagoon bottom can be uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a local Greek chef at a traditional farmhouse or culinary studio near the resort. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, fresh tzatziki, and baklava using locally sourced and seasonal ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local olive grove and artisan food producer for a premium tasting experience – sample extra virgin olive oils, aged local cheeses, thyme honey, and sun-dried tomatoes. Purchase artisan products to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely evening at the resort. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at the beach bar watching the golden hour light on the sea, followed by dinner at the resort's premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – full spread with fresh pastries, cold cuts, local cheeses, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of the morning cooking class – a sit-down meal of the dishes prepared, paired with local wine
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining – fresh sea bream en papillote with capers and lemon, roasted vegetables, and Greek orange cake with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be booked in advance and typically lasts 3–4 hours including the meal. This is a fantastic immersive food experience aligned with your culinary interests.

day_by_day.morning: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit – depart early for Zakynthos (if not already there) via a scenic ferry or short flight. Board a premium private speedboat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches, nestled between towering white limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Navagio Beach cove – swim in the electric-blue waters, photograph the famous shipwreck, and enjoy the dramatic scenery. Continue the boat tour around the Blue Caves of Zakynthos, where sunlight refracts through the sea creating vivid blue hues inside the sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to a clifftop restaurant overlooking the Ionian Sea for a spectacular sunset dinner. Return to resort by private transfer or overnight in Zakynthos at a luxury boutique hotel if distance requires.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort or hotel before early departure – pastries, fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the private speedboat – fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, local bread, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Clifftop fine-dining restaurant in Zakynthos – grilled lobster with lemon butter, Greek salad with Zakynthian feta, and loukoumades with honey and cinnamon for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is accessible only by boat. The private speedboat experience is far superior to crowded tour boats. Book well in advance. The beach can get busy midday – arrive early for the best experience and photos.

day_by_day.morning: If overnight in Zakynthos: leisurely morning exploring Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) – visit the Venetian Castle, the Byzantine Museum, and stroll the elegant waterfront promenade. If returned to main resort: relaxed morning swim and breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Afternoon at leisure – enjoy the resort's private beach, read by the pool, or book an optional watersport activity such as jet skiing or paddleboarding.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting experience at the resort or a nearby premium wine bar – focus on Greek varietals including Assyrtiko, Moschofilero, Xinomavro, and Agiorgitiko, guided by a sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Zakynthos hotel breakfast or resort breakfast on return – full Greek spread
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort – fresh salads, grilled chicken souvlaki, and freshly squeezed lemonade
meals.dinner: Premium seafood dinner at a waterfront restaurant near the resort – whole grilled fish, stuffed squid, and Greek dessert platter with loukoumades, galaktoboureko, and fresh fruit

day_by_day.notes: Use this as a transition and recovery day after the Zakynthos excursion. The wine tasting evening is a relaxed and refined way to deepen your appreciation of Greek viticulture.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise kayaking tour along the coastline – depart at dawn for a guided sea kayaking experience through sea caves, hidden coves, and along dramatic cliffs. A truly serene and exclusive way to experience the Aegean coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fish market with a private chef guide, select the freshest catch of the day, and have the chef prepare a bespoke lunch using your selected ingredients at a private villa kitchen or the resort's culinary studio.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive beach dinner experience – the resort arranges a private candlelit table on the beach with personalized menu, sommelier service, and ambient music as the stars emerge over the Aegean.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-kayaking snack – energy bars, bananas, and coffee; full breakfast on return to resort
meals.lunch: Chef-prepared bespoke lunch from market-fresh ingredients – could include grilled red mullet, stuffed mussels, and a seasonal vegetable medley with local olive oil
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner – chilled champagne on arrival, five-course tasting menu featuring the finest local ingredients, paired with curated Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner must be booked at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge and is weather-dependent. This is a highlight experience – ideal for a special occasion or simply an unforgettable evening.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby historic site – visit an ancient Greek archaeological site such as Delphi, Olympia, or Knossos (depending on resort location) with a private licensed archaeologist guide for an in-depth and exclusive historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the archaeological site and its museum. Enjoy a leisurely lunch in a nearby traditional village, sampling regional specialties in an authentic local setting far from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a sunset swim, followed by a casual but refined dinner at the resort's beach taverna.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Traditional village taverna lunch – slow-roasted goat, horta (wild greens), village bread, and local wine or raki
meals.dinner: Resort beach taverna – grilled swordfish, roasted potatoes with herbs, Greek salad, and chilled Assyrtiko wine

day_by_day.notes: A private guide transforms a historical site visit into a deeply enriching experience. Pre-book skip-the-line tickets. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a hat and water as the sites are exposed to the sun.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury yacht half-day charter – depart from the local marina on a private sailing yacht. Cruise along the most scenic stretches of coastline, anchoring at two or three exclusive swimming spots. Enjoy champagne and fresh fruit on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from yacht charter. Afternoon spa session at the resort – indulge in a full spa package including a facial, body wrap, and relaxation pool access. Completely unwind and recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at the resort's flagship restaurant – a celebration of Greek cuisine with a curated multi-course tasting menu and wine pairing by the resort's head sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, Greek pastries, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet yacht lunch – charcuterie boards, smoked fish, fresh vegetables, artisan cheeses, and chilled rosé on the deck
meals.dinner: Multi-course tasting menu at the resort's flagship restaurant – highlights include sea urchin crostini, slow-braised lamb with kritharaki, and a chocolate and mastiha mousse dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is one of the most indulgent days of the trip. The combination of a yacht charter and spa day followed by a premium dinner creates a perfect luxury experience. Book the yacht and spa in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final full morning – sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast at the resort, and take one last swim in the warm Aegean Sea from the private beach. Collect final souvenirs and artisan food products from the resort boutique or a nearby local shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: visit a local beachside café or artisan market in the nearest town. Alternatively, enjoy a final poolside afternoon with cocktails, light reading, and relaxation. Optional short hike to a scenic viewpoint overlooking the sea for a panoramic farewell view.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at a highly regarded local restaurant away from the resort – experience authentic Greek hospitality and cuisine in a traditional setting, toasting to the end of an unforgettable trip.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final resort breakfast – full spread with all favorites, fresh pastries, and a glass of fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Light mezze lunch at a beachside café – dips, pita, stuffed vine leaves, and a glass of crisp local white wine
meals.dinner: Celebrated local restaurant – whole grilled fish, seasonal vegetable dishes, local wine, and a dessert of fresh seasonal fruit with mastiha liqueur

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags the night before departure. Confirm return transfer or taxi to the airport with the concierge. Exchange any remaining local currency and settle any outstanding resort charges this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – enjoy a last Greek breakfast at the resort. Take a short final walk along the beach or sit on the terrace with a coffee and soak in the views one last time before checking out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to the airport. Depart Greece with extraordinary memories, artisan food souvenirs, and a deep appreciation for Greek culture, cuisine, and coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. In-flight relaxation after an exceptional 13-day premium Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – keep it light and enjoyable; Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and a strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge lunch or light snack before boarding
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-out, transfer, and airport procedures. The resort concierge can arrange all departure logistics. Consider joining the resort's loyalty program if available for future stays.
